Sharing passion and knowledge
We educate the new generation of biomedical engineers with high quality courses in biomedical engineering in our bachelor’s and master’s programs, and for our PDEng and PhD candidates. All of the scientific staff members actively contribute to the educational programs and guide and support students in their development as scientists and engineers. Sharing knowledge, passion and experience is the most important asset of our education programs.
The curriculum is filled with the latest developments in research and hands-on projects. A clear, coherent program is offered with the opportunity for the student to choose their own specialization. In every education specialization, challenge-based learning plays an important part in learning to solve biomedical problems at present and in the future.

The Department of Biomedical Engineering offers two programs within the Bachelor College. Please mind that for these programs you need to master both the Dutch and English language.

Exchange program
Exchange students are welcome in the Master's Degree Program of Biomedical Engineering. Please read the information below thoroughly in order to have a proper application, admission and enrollment procedure.
Read more
Erasmus Program
When you are an European Master student who takes part in the European educational program of Erasmus and would like to do an exchange program in Biomedical Engineering, please take the following steps:
Take notice of the general information on exchange programs, housing, visa etc on: TU/e exchange programs
Complete admission procedure.
To fill out the learning agreement mentioned in the admission procedure you will need to make a selection from our elective courses. Please compose this selection in accordance with your home university and department. Explore our elective courses here.
Send all documents by e-mail or to the postal adress of the exchange program coordinator of the department of Biomedical Engineering:

Complete Master's program
When you would like to apply for admittance to our complete master program instead of an exchange program, you need to contact the International Office of the Eindhoven University of Technology (not directly at the Department of Biomedical Engineering).
Internship
When you wish to do a project/internship on Biomedical Engineering at TU/e, you should contact the professor of the research group of your interest to see if there are any possibilities for a project for you. This traject takes quite some time and is not always granted. So if you are indeed interested in doing a project here, please contact the professor as soon as possible.
Before you contact one of our professors please explore our research on our website.

Internship for Biomedical Engineering Master students
We would like to invite your organization to offer an internship position for Biomedical Engineering and Medical Engineering master's students at Eindhoven University of Technology.
Below you will find the key requirements for internship placements. If you agree, please complete the attached form.
Read more
Internship Requirements
Duration and credit load
The internship should last at least 14 weeks and correspond to a workload of 20 ECTS.
Learning goals and scope
The student will work on a pre-defined, independent project in the field of Biomedical Engineering that aligns with both the program’s learning objectives and your organization’s goals. The project should be sufficiently challenging and allow the student to apply knowledge and skills acquired during their studies.
Supervision
Your organization will appoint a supervisor who supports the student, monitors progress, and provides an evaluation at the end of the internship. The supervisor may maintain contact with the university as needed. Additionally, an internal supervisor from the Biomedical Engineering department will be assigned.
Departmental approval
Internships listed in our database are not pre-approved by the department. Students are not guaranteed to undertake a specific internship until they have secured an internal supervisor. When completing the form, please select one of our three clusters that best fits the project topic, as this helps students find an internal supervisor.
Workspace and facilities
The student should have access to a suitable workspace, necessary materials, systems, and relevant information within your organization to carry out the assigned project.
Evaluation and reporting
At the end of the internship, the student will submit a report or presentation detailing their results, methodology, and reflections on the learning experience. Your organization will provide an evaluation of the student to the program’s internal supervisor.
For additional information regarding legal requirements, student rights, and intellectual property, please refer to the internship agreement provided by Universiteiten van Nederland.
We appreciate your willingness to provide a valuable learning experience for Biomedical Engineering and Medical Engineering master’s students.
